incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: routing-policy econ-route triggered - high quality regression signal (qsc > 0.25 over 5m). Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/econ-route 

Oncall SRE: taking pager. pinging eng-runtime and product. 

TJ: saw the spike in the eval pipeline. quick summary: routing decided to send large portion of traffic to gptx-4-q8 (cheap quant) in us-east-1 and eval quality dropped ~0.32 absolute across live prompt-sets. 

Sumeer: I just looked at the policy change — we shipped a tweak an hour ago that adjusts cost_weight and the quality_threshold accidentally got a wrong decimal. probable root. 

Maya: metrics: routing distribution 01:12->01:48 UTC: gptx-4-q8 72%, gptx-4-fp16 18%, fallback-other 10%. Live eval traces: baseline quality 0.85 -> 0.53 median. customer reports: hallucination/formatting regressions up on several accounts. 

TJ: log snippet from router: 
```
[router] 2026-03-15T01:12:08Z id=abcd1234 policy=econ-route decision=weighted_select selected=gptx-4-q8 score_cost=0.22 score_quality=0.61 final_score=0.78
[eval] 2026-03-15T01:12:09Z id=abcd1234 quality_drop=0.33 baseline=0.86 current=0.53
```

Sumeer: here's the policy payload we pushed (typo highlighted): 
```
policy: econ-route
  cost_weight: 0.8
  quality_threshold: 0.06   # <-- intended 0.6
  fallback: cheapest_compatible
```

Maya: yep that 0.06 explains it — policy allows very low quality in exchange for cost. Oof. 

Oncall SRE: immediate mitigations: 1) disable econ-route 2) apply short override to route enterprise customers to gptx-4-fp16 3) throttle cost-based routing for 30m. Executing now. 

Oncall SRE: running command: 
```
# disable policy immediately
redwoodctl policies disable econ-route --immediate --reason "pager: quality regressions"
# override routes for affected customers
redwoodctl routing override --selector "customer in (AcmeCorp,Bookly,Ledgerly)" --model "gptx-4-fp16" --until "2026-03-15T04:00:00Z"
```

TJ: confirmed policy disabled at 2026-03-15T01:18:33Z. routing distribution normalized within ~4min after override. live evals trending back up. :white_check_mark: 

Carla (CS): pulling list of impacted customers and creating a short status note. draft: 
"We observed an internal routing policy incident that briefly routed a higher portion of traffic to a low-cost model variant, which caused quality regressions. We have disabled the policy and applied customer-specific overrides. If you saw degraded responses between 01:12-01:48 UTC, please reply and include example prompts. We're investigating and will follow up." 

Maya: preliminary impact: 3 enterprise customers with visible regression spikes (AcmeCorp, Bookly, Ledgerly). ~18k requests affected, roughly 0.7% of global traffic during window. No data exfiltration. 

Sumeer: escalation: creating a JIRA for postmortem and root cause. proposed owner TJ. Immediate action items: 1) validation for policy editor to reject quality_threshold < 0.2 2) add canary rollout for routing policy changes (5% traffic for 10m) 3) alerting rule to correlate sudden routing shifts with eval quality deltas. 

Ava (Product): agree. also add a 'dry-run' output preview in console so PMs/SEs can see routing distribution before commit. 

Oncall SRE: handoff at 02:00Z to Maya (next oncall). leaving notes in the incident channel and on the runbook. 

Maya: taking over. I'll pair with TJ to own the postmortem. ETA for postmortem draft: EOD tomorrow. 

Carla (CS): emailing affected accounts now with the draft. will post follow-up messages for any escalations. 

TJ: followups I ran: regression suite re-run vs snapshot, patched policy editor to add sanity check, added manual rollback playbook to runbook. creating a changelist to make the default quality_threshold 0.6. 

Sumeer: thanks everyone — nice quick containment. we should add a small test harness that injects a negative quality delta when policy changes to catch this in CI. 

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged and assigned. Severity: P2 currently. Postmortem JIRA: RW-INC-2026-451. 

Oncall SRE: closing slack loop. moving discussion to postmortem doc. :lock:
